% Pattern: head/in-proof/article. Facts stated by hand inside a proof, each
% with a number in math, and a proof head right after one of them, are
% items; the proof they are in still ends at its end.
% seen in the gold pilot (set X)
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1 status=here
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-1 statement/fact D(α) status=none
% want head-2 statement/fact (β) status=here
% want head-3 proof - proves=head-2
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem} Each tree is a graph. \end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\textbf{Stage D:} Note the following facts:

\noindent\textbf{Subfact D$(\alpha)$:} Each path is a tree.

\smallskip\noindent
\textbf{Fact $(\beta)$}: Each tree is connected.

\smallskip\noindent
Proof: By renaming.

So the tree is a graph.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
